name: Light Orange
lede: Light orange is a descriptive name for a pale, warm orange; the books mostly use it as a plain description rather than a named color.

sections.title: What the name means
sections.body:
In the books, *light orange* is mostly a plain description, not a fixed color. Paterson defines corabell as a light orange coral color tinted with crimson [1]. The Pigment Compendium quotes an 1869 source that describes the color of mineral kermes, an antimony pigment, as ranging from light orange to deep carmine [2].

As a system name it is firmer: the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 lists *light orange*, and Ridgway's atlas of 1912 does too, on an aged plate that is approximate [3]. Its neighbors are [[orange]], [[peach]], [[apricot]] and [[tangerine]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 59, 0.25 per cent, as photographed [4]. It peaks in the 1500s, at 1.5 times the expected rate [4]. Inside a painting it is most often an accent, as in 60 per cent of 35 paintings [4]. In Google Books the word peaks in the 1930s [5].
